task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the first member patronage return at the Rowan Yard grocery cooperative. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Rowan Yard grocery cooperative's members approved an $18,000 patronage return from the previous financial year's available surplus.
The return is calculated at 2.5% of each member's qualifying recorded purchases during that completed year.
Qualifying member purchases totaled $720,000, which produces an $18,000 allocation at the approved rate.
Half of each calculated return will be paid in cash and half issued as credit usable at the cooperative.
The cooperative's illustrative $800 purchase total produces a $20 return, divided into $10 cash and $10 store credit.
That illustration is not a named member's account and does not show the typical amount every member will receive.
The patronage calculation excludes purchases not recorded to a member account and categories excluded in the year's published purchasing rules.
The cooperative cannot retrospectively assign an unidentified cash purchase to a member merely because the person remembers shopping there.
Treasurer Fara Noll said, "This comes after we know what the year left us. It was never a discount promised on the shelf."
The return is separate from the $30 ownership share members buy when joining the cooperative.
Members retain their ownership shares after the patronage payment; the payment is not the sale or redemption of those shares.
The members' meeting kept the remainder of the available surplus for equipment replacement and working capital.
The packet supplies no guarantee of a return in future years or of the same percentage if another distribution is approved.
Member Oren Taye asked the meeting to explain the cash-credit split because members who move away may have difficulty using store credit.
Taye said, "I can see why the shop wants money to come back through the till. People should know that before calling the whole amount cash."
The approved credit expires after 12 months and cannot be exchanged for additional cash under this distribution's terms.
Members will receive a statement showing qualifying purchases, the calculation and the two forms of payment.
The cooperative has set a review period for members to query recording errors before payments are finalized.
Nonmembers may continue shopping at the same posted shelf prices but do not receive a share of this member distribution.
The grocery was founded by residents after the closure of a privately owned food shop, and its board is elected by members.
The cooperative sells local produce alongside ordinary wholesale goods, rather than limiting membership benefits to purchases from local suppliers.
The supplied distribution papers do not determine the tax treatment of a particular member's payment.

forbidden_additions: A guaranteed annual discount, fully cash payment or redemption of ownership shares.
A typical member payment inferred from the example.
Individual tax advice or credit exchange terms not supplied.
preserve: A retrospective allocation of surplus distinguished from prices and ownership capital.
The purchase-based calculation and cash-credit distinction.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
